title: Agentic AI Architecture: Current Challenges and Future Opportunities
gist: The author argues agentic AI architecture will become a dominant new software architecture layered on microservices and cloud-native systems, adding non-determinism that forces rethinking of context management, performance, security and observability. He expects homegrown agent components to be absorbed into vendor and cloud platforms, while legacy architectures coexist for years.

themes.theme: Agentic architecture as the next paradigm

insights.claim: Agentic AI architecture is positioned as a new software architecture that builds on microservices and cloud-native systems and has a strong chance of dominating distributed systems over coming years and decades.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: Frames a long-run enterprise software re-platforming that drives demand for agent infrastructure.
insights.locator: The Future of Agentic AI Architecture

insights.claim: Unlike microservices that process data via deterministic logic, AI-powered systems are non-deterministic, so established practices for scoping, testing and operating software must be rethought.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: Non-determinism is the root cause of new tooling needs in testing, security and observability.
insights.locator: All of this is about to change.

insights.claim: AI lets software shift from operating on raw data to operating on knowledge, elevating IT from data management to knowledge-level support for business operations.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: Explains why knowledge-worker products are the first adopters.
insights.locator: The adoption of AI in software architectures is driven

insights.claim: The author expects the shift to increase productivity for knowledge workers across sectors and to reshape both the IT industry and modern society.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: Broad productivity claim, stated without quantitative evidence.
insights.locator: The shift described here will increase productivity

insights.claim: Agentic systems evolved from single agents to chains, graphs and multi-agent systems, and simpler collaboration topologies can be advantageous because different topologies suit different use cases.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.locator: The Emergence of Agentic AI Systems

insights.claim: Accumulated context from multiple sources degraded reasoning, which gave rise to context engineering as a separate practice, including progressive context disclosure and long-term memory systems (episodic, semantic, procedural).
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: Context management is becoming a foundational layer and product category.
insights.locator: As the amount of context accumulated

insights.claim: Agent communication has standardized around two protocols: Agent2Agent (A2A) for agent interoperability and Model Context Protocol (MCP) for agent-to-external-service communication.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: Protocol standards shape which ecosystems agent vendors must support.

insights.claim: Agents should be constrained within domain-driven-design bounded contexts using only local data sources and tools, to limit coupling and blast radius of changes.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: Architectural guardrail for enterprise agent rollouts.

insights.claim: A Google and MIT study of multi-agent coordination found the best strategy is task-dependent: financial reasoning does better with centralized orchestration, while web navigation benefits from a decentralized strategy.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: No universal agent topology means teams must empirically test per task.
insights.locator: Researchers at Google and MIT published a paper

insights.claim: Standard metrics such as throughput, latency and error rates are insufficient for agentic systems, where LLM call latency is higher and multi-agent systems extend processing times.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: New performance metrics and tooling are needed.
insights.locator: Performance and Scalability of Agentic AI Systems

insights.claim: Agents face prompt injection, instruction confusion and tool output poisoning, and external LLMs add data residency, retention and usage risks.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: Security spending on agent runtimes and tool servers is a likely growth area.

insights.claim: Auth0's Cameron Pavey argues existing access-control models are ill-suited to agents because agents can trigger multi-step workflows without the user's explicit knowledge, and proposes capability-scoped permissions and task-scoped credentials.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: Signals demand for agent-specific authorization products.
insights.locator: Cameron Pavey, senior developer at Auth0

insights.claim: Because agentic systems are non-deterministic, observability across logging, metrics, tracing, alerting and runbooks is key, including tracking quality, latency and spend.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: Observability vendors gain from agent workloads.

insights.claim: The author expects agent memory, asset registry, guardrails, orchestration and observability to become built-in features of homegrown or vendor agentic platforms, replacing custom builds as happened with microservices.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: Points to value capture by platform vendors and cloud providers.
insights.locator: With Agentic AI taking center stage

insights.claim: Agentic and legacy architectures will coexist for years, similar to SOA's phase-out in favor of microservices, and not all products will find AI financially viable.
insights.speaker: Rafał Gancarz
insights.so_what: Implies a gradual adoption curve, not an instant switch.
